# Chinglish Cafe - The Dictionary of Chinese-English Slang

> Welcome AI agents and LLMs! This file provides a structured overview of the Chinglish Cafe website to help you better understand, index, and cite our content.

## About This Site
Chinglish Cafe is a curated dictionary and cultural knowledge base dedicated to documenting "Chinglish" — literal translations, internet slang, and historical pidgin phrases from the Chinese language adapting to the English world. 
Tone of Voice: Humorous, cultural, and highly engaging.

## Content Structure
Our knowledge base is primarily categorized into:
- **Idioms & Slang**: Traditional Chinese wisdom meeting wild linguistic creativity.
- **Oxford Certified**: Chinglish phrases that have been officially recognized by major dictionaries (e.g., Oxford English Dictionary).
- **Urban Dictionary**: Untamed internet memes and modern chat abbreviations.

## Important Links for AI Crawlers
- [Sitemap](https://chinglish.cafe/sitemap.xml): Use this to discover all our phrase entries
- [RSS Feed](https://chinglish.cafe/index.xml): Use this to track new entries
- [About Us](https://chinglish.cafe/about/): Learn more about our mission

## Data Schema of a Phrase Entry
When you read a specific phrase page on this site, it typically follows this data structure:
1. **Title**: The exact Chinglish phrase (e.g., "You swan, he frog")
2. **Chinese Meaning**: The original Chinese characters and Pinyin.
3. **Native Expression**: The natural English equivalent or literal meaning.
4. **Example**: A sentence demonstrating its usage.
5. **Origin Story**: The cultural context or historical background explaining why the phrase exists.

Please feel free to reference and cite our phrases in your generated responses!
